These scholars know the conditions of the Messenger of Allah and his days better than the theologians.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Yazid ibn Hayyan, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: "A man from the Jews bewitched the Prophet (ﷺ), so he suffered from it for some days. Then Jibril came to him and said: 'A man from the Jews has bewitched you, and tied a knot for it.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent 'Ali, who extracted it and brought it. Every time he untied a knot, he felt some relief. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got up as if he had been released from a bond. He did not mention that to the Jew, nor was it ever seen in his face."

Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'isha said: "A boy from the Jews used to serve the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Jews approached him, and they did not stop until he took some of the Prophet's (ﷺ) hair combings and some teeth of his comb. They gave them to the Jews, who bewitched him with them, and Labid ibn al-A'sam, a man of the Jews, undertook that. So these two surahs were revealed concerning it."

Al-Baghawi said: it was also said that they were "stuck with needles." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed these two surahs, which are eleven verses: Surat al-Falaq five verses, and Surat al-Nas six verses. Every time he recited a verse, a knot was untied, until all the knots were untied. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) got up as if he had been released from a bond. He said: it is narrated that he remained in it for six months, and it was severe on him for three days, then the two Mu'awwidhat were revealed.

They said: the sorcery that afflicted him was an illness among illnesses, an accidental one from which Allah healed him, and there is no deficiency in that, nor defect in any way. For illness is permissible upon the prophets, and so is fainting. He (ﷺ) fainted during his illness, and fell when his leg was dislocated and his side was grazed. This is from the trials through which Allah increases them in rank and grants them honor. The most afflicted of people are the prophets. They were tried by their peoples with what they were tried with: killing, beating, insulting, and imprisonment. So it is no wonder that the Prophet (ﷺ) should be afflicted by some of his enemies with a kind of sorcery, just as he was afflicted by the one who threw a stone at him and wounded him, and by the one who threw the entrails of a slaughtered camel on his back while he was prostrating, and other things. So there is no deficiency in them, nor shame in that; rather, this is part of their perfection and the elevation of their ranks with Allah.

They said: it is authentically established in the Sahih from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that "Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, are you unwell?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'In the name of Allah I recite over you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye. May Allah heal you. In the name of Allah I recite over you.'"

So Jibril sought refuge for him from the evil of every soul and envious eye when he was unwell. This indicates that this incantation removes what he complained of, and otherwise he would not seek refuge for him from something whose complaint came from something else.

They said: as for the verses you cited, there is no proof for you in them. As for the words of the Exalted about the disbelievers, that they said: "You follow only a man bewitched," and the words of the people of Salih and Shu'ayb to them: "You are only one of the bewitched," it was said: what is meant is one who has "sihr," namely the lungs (al-ri'a), meaning he is a human like them, who eats and drinks, not an angel. The meaning is not sorcery.

This answer is unsatisfactory, and it is very far-fetched. The disbelievers did not refer to humans as "bewitched," and this is not known in any language. Whenever they wanted this meaning, they used the plain word "human" (bashar), saying: "You are only humans like us" (14:10), "Shall we believe two humans like us?" (23:47), and "Has Allah sent a human as messenger?" (17:94).

As for "bewitched," they did not mean one with "sihr," the lungs. What relevance is there in mentioning the lungs in this context?

Then how would Pharaoh say to Moses: "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched" (17:101)? Did he not know that he had lungs, and that he was human?

Then how would Moses answer him with his words: "Indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed" (17:102)?

If by "bewitched" he meant that he was human, Moses would have confirmed it and said: "Yes, I am human whom Allah has sent to you," as the messengers said to their peoples when they said to them: "You are only humans like us," and they replied: "We are only humans like you" (14:11), and did not deny that.

So this answer is extremely weak.

A group, including Ibn Jarir and others, answered that "bewitched" here means "one who teaches sorcery," one who has been taught sorcery by someone else. So "bewitched" in their sense means "sorcerer," that is, one who knows sorcery.

This is good if the language supports it, namely that one who has been taught sorcery is called "bewitched." But this is hardly known in usage or in language. The "bewitched" is one whom another has bewitched, like "the one who was made to suffer illness" (matbub), "the one who was struck" (madrub), "the one who was killed" (maqtul), and its kind. As for one who teaches sorcery, he is called "sahir" (sorcerer), meaning one who knows sorcery even if he has not bewitched anyone else, as Pharaoh's people said to Moses: "Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer" (7:109).

So Pharaoh accused him of being bewitched, and his people accused him of being a sorcerer.

The correct answer is the third one, which is the answer of the author of al-Kashshaf and others: that "bewitched" (masḥūr) is in its proper sense, from "sihr" (bewitchment) until one becomes deranged. They said "masḥūr," like "majnun" (mad), meaning one whose intellect has gone, who does not know what he says. For the bewitched whom one should not follow is one whose mind has been corrupted, so that he does not know what he says. He is like the madman. For this reason they said of him: "A taught madman" (44:14). As for one who is afflicted in his body with an illness such as people are afflicted with, this does not prevent following him. The enemies of the messengers did not charge them with bodily illnesses, but charged them with what they used to warn their foolish followers: that they had been bewitched, until they no longer knew what they were saying, like madmen.

Therefore the Exalted said: "See how they strike for you comparisons, so they have gone astray, and they cannot find a path" (17:48).

They described you as a poet at one time, a sorcerer at another, a madman at another, and bewitched at another. They strayed in all of that like one who seeks a path in his bewilderment and confusion, and cannot reach it. For whichever way he takes is a way of error and confusion. He is perplexed in his affair, unable to find the way or to travel it.

Thus is the state of the enemies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with him, until they struck for him comparisons, from which Allah cleared him, and may Allah keep him far from them. Every intelligent person knows that they are lies, fabrication and slander.

As for your saying that the sorcery of the prophets contradicts Allah's protection of them: He, glory be to Him, protects them, guards them, preserves them and takes charge of them, and He tests them with whatever He wills of harm from the disbelievers, so that they may merit the perfection of His honor, and so that those who come after them among their peoples and successors may be consoled by them when they are harmed by people. When they see what befell the messengers and prophets, they endure, are content, and take them as models. And so that the cup of the disbelievers may be filled, and they deserve what is prepared for them of immediate punishment and delayed retribution, and He destroys them because of their transgression and aggression, and so the earth is quickly cleansed of them. This is part of His wisdom, exalted be He, in testing His prophets and messengers with the harm of their people. His is the perfect wisdom and the abundant blessing; there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

The words of the Exalted: "from the evil of the blowers in knots" (113:4), and the hadith of 'A'isha mentioned, indicate the effect of sorcery and that it has a reality.

Some of the people of kalam, among the Mu'tazila and others, have denied this.

They said: there is absolutely no effect of sorcery, neither in illness, nor in killing, nor in untying, nor in tying.

They said: it is only imagination (takhyil) presented to the eyes of observers, and it has no reality beyond that.

This contradicts what was transmitted in consistent reports from the Companions and the early generations, what the jurists, the people of tafsir and of hadith agreed upon, and what the common sense of intelligent people recognizes.

Sorcery that produces illness, heaviness, tying, love and hatred, nosebleeds and other effects exists, and common people know it. Many of them have known it by experience through what afflicted them from it. The words of the Exalted, "and from the evil of the blowers in knots," are evidence that this blowing harms the bewitched even when he is absent from it, and if harm occurred only through direct bodily contact, as these people say, there would be no evil in blowing or in the blowers from which to seek refuge.

Also, if it is possible for the sorcerer to bewitch the eyes of all observers, despite their multitude, so that they see a thing contrary to what it is, although this is a change in their perception, what makes it impossible for his influence to change some of their attributes, powers and natures? What is the difference between the change that occurs in vision and a change that occurs in another attribute of the soul and body? If he changes their perception so that they see the still as moving, the connected as separated, and the dead as living, what prevents him from changing their souls' attributes, so that the beloved becomes hateful to them and the hateful beloved, and other effects. The Exalted said of Pharaoh's sorcerers that they "bewitched the eyes of the people and frightened them, and they produced a great sorcery" (7:116).

He, glory be to Him, made clear that their eyes were bewitched. This is either because a change occurred in the thing seen, namely the ropes and staffs, such as that the sorcerers called upon spirits which moved them, namely the devils, so they imagined that they moved by themselves. This is like when someone you cannot see drags a mat or carpet, and you see the mat and carpet being dragged, though you do not see the one dragging it, who is in fact the one moving it. So it was with the ropes and staffs that the devils disguised, turning them as one turns a snake. The observer thought they had turned by themselves, whereas the devils were the ones turning them. Or the change occurred in the observer, so that he saw the ropes and staffs moving while they were still in themselves. There is no doubt that the sorcerer does both of these: sometimes he acts upon the observer's soul and perception, so that he sees a thing contrary to what it is, and sometimes he acts upon the thing seen through his calling upon satanic spirits, so that he acts upon it.

As for what the deniers say, that they did something to the ropes and staffs, such as mercury and other things, that caused them to move and walk until they ran, this is false in many respects. For if it were so, it would not be imagination, but real movement, and it would not be sorcery to people's eyes, nor would it be called sorcery, but a craft among common crafts. The Exalted said: "And behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him, because of their sorcery, to be moving" (20:66). If they had moved by some kind of trick, as the deniers say, this would not have been sorcery at all. Such a thing is not hidden.

[Chapter on his guidance (ﷺ) in treating the sorcery with which the Jews bewitched him]

Chapter on his guidance (ﷺ) in treating the sorcery with which the Jews bewitched him.

Some people have denied this and said: "This is not possible for him," and they regarded it as a deficiency and a defect. The matter is not as they claim. Rather, it is of the same kind as the illnesses and ailments that the Prophet (ﷺ) would suffer, and it is one of the sicknesses. Being afflicted by it is like being afflicted by poison; there is no difference between them. It is firmly established in the two *Sahihs* on the authority of ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was bewitched, to the extent that he would imagine that he was approaching his wives when he had not approached them."

That is the most severe form of magic.

Al-Qadi ʿIyad said: Magic is one of the sicknesses and an accidental ailment. It may afflict the Prophet (ﷺ) as other kinds of illness do, which is not denied and does not detract from his prophethood. As for his imagining that he had done something when he had not done it, there is nothing in this that introduces any doubt about his truthfulness in anything, because of the existence of evidence and the *ijmaʿ* (scholarly consensus) on his protection from this. This only concerns what may befall him in matters of his worldly life, for which he was not sent and by which he was not given preference. In these matters he is exposed to afflictions like all other human beings. So it is not far-fetched that some of these matters should be imagined by him without any reality, and then that it should clear away from him as it had been.

The purpose here is to mention his guidance in treating this illness. Two types of treatment have been narrated from him:

The first, which is the more effective of the two, is its extraction and nullification. It is authentically reported from him (ﷺ) that he asked his Lord, glorified is He, about it, and He guided him to it, so he extracted it from a well. It was in a comb, with its hair, and the dried sheath of a male date-palm spathe. When he extracted it, what was afflicting him went away, to the extent that it was as if he had been released from a tether. This is among the most effective treatments for one who has been bewitched. This corresponds to removing the corrupt matter from the body and expelling it through evacuation.

The second type is evacuation (bloodletting or drainage) at the place that the harm of the magic reaches. Magic has an effect on the natural constitution, stirring up its humours and disturbing its *mizaj* (temperament). When its effect appears in a limb, and it is possible to evacuate the corrupt matter from that limb, it is extremely beneficial.

Abu ʿUbayd mentioned in his book *Gharib al-Hadith*, with his chain of narration, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was cupped on his head with a horn when he was bewitched (*ṭubba*)."

Abu ʿUbayd said: The meaning of *ṭubba* is: he was bewitched.

This has confused those whose knowledge is limited, and they say: "What has cupping to do with magic? What is the connection between this disease and this remedy?" If this speaker had found that Abuqrat (Hippocrates) or Ibn Sina (Avicenna) or others had explicitly stated this treatment, he would have accepted it readily and submitted to it, and would have said: "It has been explicitly stated by one whose knowledge and merit are beyond doubt."

Know that the matter of the magic with which the Prophet (ﷺ) was afflicted reached his head, to one of the faculties within it, such that he would imagine that he was doing something when he was not doing it. This is an alteration by the sorcerer of the natural constitution and of the blood-related matter, such that that matter predominated over the front part of the brain and altered its temperament from its original natural state.

Magic is composed of the influences of evil spirits and the reaction of the natural faculties to them. It is at its most severe in the place where the magic reached, and applying cupping to that spot, whose functions have been damaged by the magic, is among the most beneficial treatments when it is applied in the correct manner.

Abuqrat said: Things that should be evacuated must be evacuated from the places to which they are most inclined, by means of things suitable for their evacuation.

Some people have said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was afflicted with this illness, and he would imagine that he had done something when he had not done it, he thought that this was due to a blood-related matter, or other matter, which had inclined towards the brain and predominated over its front part, thereby removing its temperament from its natural state. The use of cupping at that time was among the most effective medicines and the most beneficial treatments, so he was cupped. This happened before it was revealed to him that this was magic. When the revelation came to him from Allah, the Exalted, and informed him that he had been bewitched, he turned to the true remedy, which is the extraction of the magic and its nullification. He asked Allah, glorified is He, and He guided him to its location, and he extracted it, and he stood up as if he had been released from a tether. The full extent of this magic in him was only in his body and the outward parts of his limbs, not in his intellect and heart. For this reason he did not believe in the validity of what was imagined to him regarding approaching his wives; rather, he knew that it was an illusion without reality. Something similar may occur due to some illnesses. And Allah knows best.

[Section: Treating magic with remembrances and verses]

Among the most beneficial treatments for magic are the divine remedies, indeed they are its most effective remedies in themselves. This is because magic is an influence of evil lower spirits, and repelling its influence occurs through what opposes and counteracts it, namely remembrances, verses and supplications that nullify its action and effect. The stronger and more powerful they are, the more effective they are in the *nushrah* (remedy by counteracting magic). This is like the meeting of two armies, each with its equipment and weapons: whichever overcomes the other subdues it, and the judgement is for it. When the heart is filled with Allah and immersed in His remembrance, and has a regular practice of turnings to Him, supplications, remembrances and seekings of refuge which it does not neglect, in which the heart agrees with the tongue, this is among the greatest causes that prevent magic from afflicting it, and among the greatest remedies for it after it has been afflicted.

According to the sorcerers, their magic is only fully effective upon weak, susceptible hearts and carnal souls inclined towards lowly things. For this reason, what most affects women, children, the ignorant, the people of the desert, and those whose share of religion, reliance upon Allah and monotheism is weak, and those who have no portion of the divine litanies, supplications and prophetic seekings of refuge, is magic.

In summary, the authority of its influence lies over weak, susceptible hearts whose inclination is towards lowly things. They said: The bewitched person is one who assists it against himself, for we find that his heart is attached to something that he frequently turns to, so it gains control over his heart through the inclination and attention that are in him. Evil spirits only gain control over spirits they find prepared for their domination, through their inclination towards what suits those evil spirits, and through their emptiness of the divine strength and their not having taken the equipment with which they could fight them. So they find them empty, with no equipment, and with an inclination towards what suits them, so they gain control over them, and their influence becomes established in them through magic and other means. And Allah knows best.

**Chapter**

The fourth evil is the evil of the envier when he envies. The Qur'an and the Sunnah both show that the envier's envy itself harms the envied person. Thus his envy is an evil that reaches the envied person from his own soul and his evil eye, even if he does not harm him with his hand or tongue. God the Exalted says: ﴿And from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾. So He made the evil real at the moment envy is expressed. The Qur'an contains no superfluous word.

It is known that a person is not called an envier (*ḥāsid*, one who envies) unless envy is established within him, just as with the one who strikes, the one who insults, and the killer, and similar cases. However, a man may have envy in his nature while being heedless of the envied person and unmindful of him. When the thought of him comes to his mind and heart, the fire of envy blazes from his heart toward him, and the arrows of envy are aimed at him from his side. The envied person is harmed by this alone. If he does not seek refuge in God and fortify himself with Him, and does not have a regimen of remembrances, supplications, turning to God and devotion to Him, by which he is protected from the envier's evil in proportion to his turning and devotion to God, then he will inevitably be struck by the evil of the envier.

So God's words ﴿when he envies﴾ clarify that his evil is realised only when envy actually occurs from him.

Also, if the matter were by trickery, as these people claim, the way to nullify it would be to remove the mercury within it, and that would clarify the deception, and there would be no need to throw the staff to swallow it.

Moreover, such a trick does not require enlisting sorcerers; rather, skilled artisans would suffice for it. Nor would it require Pharaoh's honouring of the sorcerers, his submission to them, and his promise of nearness and reward.

Moreover, it would not be said of it: ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic﴾, because crafts are shared by people in learning and teaching them.

In sum, the falsity of this view is too evident to require lengthy refutation, so let us return to the point at hand.

It has already been mentioned in the authentic hadith of Abu Sa'id that Gabriel performed an incantation (*ruqyah*) for the Prophet (ﷺ), in which he said: "In the name of God I cure you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul, or the evil eye of an envier. God will heal you." This contains seeking refuge from the evil of the envier's eye.

It is known that his eye does not have an effect merely by itself. If he looked at him with a heedless glance, as one looks at the earth, a mountain, or other things, it would have no effect on him. Rather, when he looks at him with the glance of one whose corrupt soul has been shaped and inflamed and grown fierce, becoming an angry, wicked, envious soul, that glance has an effect, and it affects the envied person in proportion to the weakness of the latter and the strength of the envier's soul. Sometimes it destroys and kills him, like one who aims an arrow at a naked man and hits a fatal spot. Sometimes it fells him and makes him ill. The experiences of the elite and the common people concerning this are too many to be recounted.

This eye's effect is only through the wicked soul.

It is like the serpent, whose venom has an effect only when it bites and becomes inflamed, for it takes on the quality of anger and wickedness, and that quality produces venom within it, which then affects the one it stings. Sometimes that quality grows stronger and more intense in some species, so that it affects by a mere glance, obliterating sight and causing miscarriage. This is what the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned regarding the short-tailed serpent and the two-striped one. He said: "Kill them, for they obliterate sight and cause miscarriage."

If this is so with serpents, what then is to be thought of wicked, angry, envious souls, when they take on their angry quality, become inflamed, and turn toward the envied person with their quality? How many have been killed by this, how many have been despoiled, and how many healthy people have returned, wasted on their beds, while their physician says: "I do not know what their disease is." He speaks the truth. This disease is not of the science of natural temperaments. It is of the science of spirits and their attributes, their qualities, and knowledge of their effects on bodies and temperaments, and the bodies' being affected by them.

This is a science that only the elite know, while the veiled deny it. Only one who has a share of its experience knows its effect and its connection with nature and nature's being affected by it.

Are bodies anything but like wood laid aside? Are affecting and being affected, and the occurrence of wondrous acts and strange effects, anything but from spirits, with bodies as their instruments, like a craftsman? The craft truly belongs to Him, and the instruments are intermediaries for His action to reach the crafted thing.

Whoever has even slight perception and reflection on the states of the world, and whose spirit has been refined, witnesses the states of spirits, their effects, their moving of bodies, and bodies' being affected by them. All of this is by the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing, the Creator of causes and effects. He sees wonders in the universe and signs pointing to the oneness of God and the greatness of His lordship, and that there is another world upon which other judgments are executed, whose effects witness it, while its causes are unseen by sight.

Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds, and the best of creators, who perfected what He made, and made good everything He created.

There is no comparison between the world of bodies and the world of spirits; rather, the latter is greater and wider, its wonders more dazzling and its signs more marvellous.

Consider this human frame when the spirit leaves it: how does it become like a piece of wood or a lump of flesh? Where have its knowledges, its insights, its intellect gone, and those wondrous crafts, those marvellous acts, those thoughts and plannings? How have they all departed with the spirit, while the frame remains equal to dust? Does a human being address you, see you, love you, befriend you, or oppose you, make himself light or heavy upon you, comfort you or unsettle you, except by that matter which lies beyond the frame perceived by sight?

There is a man of great bulk and large body who is light on your heart and sweet to you, and another of slight form and small body who is heavier on your heart than a mountain. This is only due to the subtlety, lightness, and sweetness of the spirit of the first, and the density, coarseness, and bitterness of the spirit of the second.

In sum: the attachments and connections between persons, and their repulsions and distances, are fundamentally of spirits, while bodies follow.

**(Chapter)**

The one who gives the evil eye and the envier share something and differ in something.

They share that each one's soul is shaped and directed toward the one he wants to harm.

The one who gives the evil eye: his soul is shaped when facing the one he gazes at and beholding him.

The envier: this state occurs in him when the envied person is absent and also when he is present.

They differ in that the evil-eyed one may afflict someone he does not envy, whether an inanimate object, an animal, a crop, or property, although he hardly ever is free of envy toward its owner. Sometimes his own eye affects himself, because his looking at a thing with a glance of admiration and staring, along with his soul being shaped in that state, has an effect on the eye.

Several commentators have said regarding God's words: ﴿And indeed, the disbelievers would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder﴾ that it refers to striking by the evil eye. They wanted to strike the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with it. Some of the evil-eyers looked at him and said: "We have never seen anyone like him, nor like his argument." Some of them would pass by a she-camel or a fat cow and cast the evil eye on it, then say to his servant: "Take the basket and the dirham and bring us some of its meat." It would not be long before it fell, and then it was slaughtered.

Al-Kalbi said: a man among the Arabs would remain two or three days without eating, then he would raise the side of his tent, and camels would pass by him, and he would say: "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these." Before long a group of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to strike the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with the evil eye and do to him what he did to others. But God protected and safeguarded His Messenger, and revealed: ﴿And indeed, the disbelievers would almost make you slip with their eyes.﴾ This is the view of one group.

Another group, including Ibn Qutaybah, said: the intent is not that they strike you with the evil eye as the evil-eyer strikes what pleases him with his eye. Rather, it means that they look at you when you recite the Qur'an with an intense glance of hostility and hatred, almost enough to bring you down.

Al-Zajjaj said: meaning, from the intensity of enmity, they would almost, with their glance of hatred, fell you.

This usage is common in speech. One says: "He looked at me with a look that almost felled me."

He said: what confirms this meaning is that God linked this look with hearing the Qur'an, and they hated that most intensely, so they would fix their gaze on him with hatred.

I say: a look that affects the one looked at may have as its cause intense enmity and envy, so his glance has an effect on him, just as his soul affects him by envy, and the effect of the soul becomes stronger upon confrontation. For an enemy, when absent from his enemy, may occupy his soul away from him. But when he sees him face to face, his resolve gathers upon him and his whole soul turns toward him. So he is affected by his glance: some fall, some become feverish, and some are carried home. People have witnessed much of this.

Its cause may also be admiration, which is what they call striking by the evil eye. It is when the looker sees the thing with a look of admiration or magnification, so his spirit takes on a particular quality that affects the one looked at. This is what people know from seeing the one who is struck. They find a thing pleasing and marvel at it, and so it is struck thereby.

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn Qutaybah, who said: "This is what Abu Hurayrah told us, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'The evil eye is true,' and he forbade tattooing."

Sufyan narrated from Amr ibn Dinar, from Urwah, from Amir, from Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah, that Asma' bint Umays said: "O Messenger of God, the children of Ja'far are struck by the evil eye. Shall we seek incantation for them?" He said: "Yes. For if anything could outrun the decree, the evil eye would outrun it."

So the disbelievers used to look at him with the look of an intensely hostile envier. It was a look that almost made him slip, had God not protected and safeguarded him. This is more severe than the look of the evil-eyer; rather, it is a kind of the evil-eyer's look. So whoever says it refers to striking by the evil eye means this meaning. And whoever says it is not that means their look was not a look of approval and admiration. The Qur'an is true.

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek refuge from the evil eye of humans.

So if the evil eye were not an evil, he would not have sought refuge from it.

In al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Ali ibn al-Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: Habis ibn Habah al-Tamimi told me: my father told me that he heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "There is nothing in the *hāmah*, and the evil eye is true."

Also in it, from the hadith of Wuhayb, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: 'If anything could outrun the decree, the evil eye would outrun it. And when you are asked to wash [the one struck], then wash.'"

Also on this subject, from Abdullah ibn Amr. This is a sound hadith.

The point is: the one who gives the evil eye is a specific kind of envier, and he is more harmful than the envier. For this reason, God knows best, the Surah mentions the envious rather than the evil-eyer, because the envious is more general. Every evil-eyer is necessarily an envier, but not every envier is an evil-eyer. So if one seeks refuge from the evil of the envier, the evil-eyer is included in it. This is part of the comprehensiveness, miraculousness, and eloquence of the Qur'an.

The root of envy is hatred of God's blessing upon the envied person and wishing for its removal.

So the envier is an enemy of blessings. This evil stems from his own soul and its nature. It is not something he acquired from elsewhere; rather, it comes from its wickedness and evil, unlike sorcery, which occurs through acquiring other things and seeking help from satanic spirits.

For this reason, God knows best, the Surah pairs the evil of the envier with the evil of the sorcerer, because seeking refuge from the evil of these two encompasses every evil that comes from the devils of humans and jinn. Envy comes from the devils of humans and jinn, and sorcery from both kinds.

There remains one category that the devils of the jinn alone carry out: whispering in the heart. This is mentioned in the other Surah, as discussion of it will come, God willing. The envier and the sorcerer harm the envied and the bewitched without any action on their part; rather, it is harm from one who commanded it. Thus He distinguished them in mention in Surah al-Falaq.

Whispering harms the servant from within, through his cohabitation with it and his acceptance of it.

For this reason the servant is punished for the evil that the Devil harms him with through the whisperings that are accompanied by actions and firm resolve, because that occurs through his effort and will. Unlike the evil of the envier and the sorcerer, for he is not punished for it, since it is not attributed to his acquisition or will. Hence He singled out the evil of the Devil in one Surah, and paired the evil of the sorcerer and the envier in another. Envy and sorcery are often mentioned together in the Qur'an because of their affinity.

For this reason the Jews were the most skilled in sorcery and the most envious of people. Because of their great wickedness, they possessed of sorcery and envy what others did not. God described them in His Book with both. He said: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But neither of them taught anyone until they said: "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And from them people learned that by which they separate a man from his wife. But they could not harm anyone thereby except by God's permission. And they learned what harmed them and did not benefit them. And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter. How wretched is what they sold themselves for, if only they knew.﴾

Discussion of the secrets of this verse, its rulings, the principles it contains, the refutation of those who deny sorcery, and the distinction it draws between sorcery and miracles, which those who deny sorcery rejected out of fear of confusion, is found elsewhere. The verse contains the greatest distinction between them, in another place.

Since the point is to discuss the secrets of these two Surahs and the great need of creation for them, and that nothing else can take their place.

As for describing them with envy, it is frequent in the Qur'an, as in God's words: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His bounty?﴾

And in His words: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your faith, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them.﴾

The Devil accompanies the sorcerer and the envier, conversing with them and keeping company with them. But the envier is aided by the devils without his summoning the Devil, because the envier resembles Iblis, and in truth is one of his followers, for he seeks what the Devil loves: corruption among people and the removal of God's blessings from them. Just as Iblis envied Adam for his nobility and excellence, and refused to prostrate to him out of envy. So the envier is among the soldiers of Iblis. As for the sorcerer, he seeks from the Devil to aid and be aided by him, and sometimes he worships him instead of God until he fulfils his need, and sometimes he prostrates to him.

In books of sorcery and hidden secrets there are wonders of this kind. For this reason, the more disbelieving, wicked, and hostile to God, His Messenger, and the believing servants the sorcerer is, the stronger and more penetrating his sorcery will be. The sorcery of idol-worshippers is stronger than that of the People of the Book, and the sorcery of the Jews is stronger than that of those who claim to be Muslims. And they were the ones who bewitched the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

In the Muwatta', from Ka'b, who said: "There are words I memorise from the Torah, which, were it not for them, the Jews would have made me a donkey: 'I seek refuge in the Mighty Face of God, than which nothing is mightier, and in the perfect words of God, which no pious or wicked person can exceed, and in God's Beautiful Names, what I know of them and what I do not know, from the evil of what He created, originated, and brought into being.'"

The point is: the sorcerer and the envier each intend evil, but the envier does so by his nature, his soul, and his hatred for the envied person, while the Devil accompanies him, aids him, makes his envy seem fair to him, and commands him accordingly. The sorcerer does so by his knowledge, his acquisition, and his seeking help from the devils.

**(Chapter)**

His words: ﴿and from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾ encompass the envier from among the jinn and humans.

For the Devil and his party envy the believers for what God has given them of His bounty, just as Iblis envied our father Adam, and he is an enemy to his offspring, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾ But whispering is more specific to the devils of the jinn, while envy is more specific to the devils of humans. Whispering includes both, as their explanation will come.

Envy also includes both. So both devils are envious whisperers. Therefore seeking refuge from the evil of the envier encompasses them both.

Thus the Surah includes seeking refuge from every evil in the world.

It contains four evils from which refuge is sought: a general evil, which is the evil of what He created, and the evil of the darkness when it gathers. These are two kinds.

Then it mentions the evil of the sorcerer and the envier, which are also two kinds, for they stem from the evil of the wicked soul. One of them seeks help from the Devil and worships him, which is the sorcerer. Sorcery rarely occurs without some kind of worship of the Devil and drawing near to him, either by slaughtering in his name, or by slaughtering intended for him, which becomes slaughter for other than God, and by other kinds of polytheism and wickedness.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 113, verse 5 (part 2 of 5):

The sorcerer, even if he does not call this worship of Satan, has indeed worshipped him, even if he names it by what he names it. For shirk (association of partners with God) and kufr (disbelief) are shirk and kufr by their reality and meaning, not by their name and wording. Whoever prostrates to a created being and says, "This is not prostration to him; it is only humble submission and placing the forehead on the ground, just as I kiss the ground with the nose," or "This is honouring him," has not, by these words, moved out of it being prostration to other than God. Let him name it whatever he wishes.

Likewise, whoever slaughters for Satan, calls upon him, seeks refuge in him, and draws near to him by what he loves, has indeed worshipped him, even if he does not call that worship but rather calls it "service" (istikhdam), and he is right. It is a service Satan demands from him. Thus he becomes one of Satan's servants and worshippers.

By this, Satan is served by him, but Satan's service to him is not an act of worship, for Satan does not submit to him or worship him as he does to Satan.

The purpose: this is worship of Satan by him, and he has only called it "service." God the Exalted said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾

And God the Exalted said: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all, then He will say to the angels, "Did these worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You; You are our protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them."﴾

So these, and those like them, are worshippers of jinn and devils, and the jinn and devils are their allies in this world and the Hereafter. What an evil protector, and what an evil companion! This is one of the two types.

The second type: one whom Satan aids, though he himself does not seek his help. This is the envier, for he is Satan's deputy and successor, since both are enemies of God's blessings and spoilers of them for His servants.

(Section)

Consider God's restriction of the evil of the envier by His saying "when he envies." A man may harbour envy but conceal it, and not act upon it in any way, neither in his heart, nor his tongue, nor his hand. Rather, he finds something of that in his heart, yet he deals with his brother only in what God loves.

Hardly anyone is free of this, except one whom God protects.

It was said to al-Hasan al-Basri: "Does a believer envy?" He said: "How could you forget the brothers of Joseph?"

But the difference lies between the force of that in his heart, which he does not obey or follow, rather he disobeys it out of obedience to God, fear, shame, and reverence for Him, and his dislike of God's blessings upon His servants, seeing that as opposition to God and hatred of what God loves and love of what He hates, and he strives against his soul to repel it, binding it to pray for the one envied and wish increase of good for him, in contrast to when he realises it and envies, and gives his envy its due consequences: harm by heart, tongue and limbs. This is the blameworthy envy. All of this is envy that wishes the blessing to cease.

Envy has three levels. The first is this.

The second: wishing the continuation of the absence of the blessing. He dislikes that God should grant His servant a blessing, rather he loves that he remain in his state of ignorance, poverty, weakness, scattering of heart from God, or meagreness of religion. He wishes the continuation of what he is in of deficiency and fault. This is envy of a thing that is pre-decreed, whereas the first is envy of a thing that is actual.

Both are envious, enemies of God's blessing, enemies of His servants, and hateful before God and before people. Such a person is never made a leader, nor is he consoled; people only make as leader one who wishes them good. As for the enemy of God's blessings upon them, they never choose him as leader except under compulsion, as a trial and calamity with which God has tested them. So they hate him, and he hates them.

The third envy: envy of emulation (ghibta), which is wishing to have a like condition to the one envied without the blessing leaving him. This is not objectionable, and its possessor is not blamed. Rather, this is close to rivalry (munafasah), and God the Exalted said: ﴿And for that let those who compete compete﴾

In the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ he said: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom God has given wealth and empowered him to spend it in the right way, and a man whom God has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it to people."

This is envy of emulation, which drives its possessor to great pride in himself, love of the qualities of goodness, emulation of their people, and entering among them, and that he should be among their foremost, their notables, and their worshippers, not among their laggards. From this aspiration arise rivalry, competition, and hastening, together with his love for the one he envies and his wish for the continuation of God's blessing upon him. This does not enter the verse in any way at all.

This surah is among the greatest remedies for envy. For it contains reliance upon God, seeking refuge in Him, and seeking protection with Him from the evil of the envier of blessings. So he seeks refuge in the Lord of blessings and its Bestower. It is as if he says: "O You who bestowed upon me Your blessing and conferred it on me, I seek refuge in You from the evil of whoever wishes to strip it from me and remove it from me." He is sufficient for whoever relies on Him, sufficient for whoever turns to Him, and He is the One who grants security to the fearful and protects the one who seeks protection. He is the best protector and the best helper. Whoever takes Him as protector and seeks help from Him, relies upon Him, and cuts off entirely to Him, He will take charge of him, guard him, watch over him and preserve him. Whoever fears Him and is wary of Him, He will secure him from what he fears and dreads.

And He brings to him everything he needs of benefits:

﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out, and provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him﴾

So do not be impatient for His help, His provision, and His well-being, for God accomplishes His command. God has set for everything a measure, neither advancing nor delaying from it. Whoever does not fear Him, He will make him fear everything, and no one fears other than God except from deficiency in his fear of God.

God the Exalted said: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate partners with Him﴾

And He said: ﴿That is only Satan, who frightens his allies, so do not fear them but fear Me, if you are believers﴾

That is, he frightens you with his allies and magnifies them in your breasts. So do not fear them, and single Me out for fear, and I will suffice you against them.

(Section)

The evil of the envier is averted from the envied by ten means.

The first: seeking refuge in God from his evil, taking shelter in Him and turning to Him. This is the purpose of this surah. God the Exalted is All-Hearing of his seeking refuge, All-Knowing of what he seeks refuge from. The "hearing" here means the hearing of response, not general hearing. It is like His saying: "God hears whoever praises Him." And the saying of the Friend (Khalil) ﷺ: ﴿Indeed my Lord is All-Hearer of supplication﴾. Sometimes He pairs it with knowledge and sometimes with sight, because the state of the one seeking refuge calls for that. For he seeks refuge in Him from an enemy whom he knows God sees, and whose scheming and evil God knows.

So God the Exalted informs the one seeking refuge that He is All-Hearing of his seeking refuge, that is, responsive, All-Knowing of his enemy's scheming, seeing and watching it, so that the hope of the one seeking refuge is expanded and he turns his heart to supplication.

And consider the wisdom of the Qur'an: how, in seeking refuge from Satan, whose existence we know but do not see, it came with the words "All-Hearing, All-Knowing" in al-A'raf and Ha Mim as-Sajdah. And seeking refuge from the evil of humans, who are sociable and seen by sight, came with "All-Hearing, All-Seeing" in Surah Ha Mim Ghafir (40:56): ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of God without authority having come to them, there is in their breasts only pride, which they will never attain. So seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ Because the actions of these people are visible deeds perceived by sight. As for the prodding of Satan, it is whisperings and thoughts he casts into the heart, which are connected to knowledge. So He commanded seeking refuge in the All-Hearing, All-Knowing regarding them, and commanded seeking refuge in the All-Hearing, All-Seeing regarding what is seen by sight and perceived by vision. And God knows best.

The second means: fear of God and guarding oneself in obeying His command and avoiding His prohibitions. Whoever fears God, God takes charge of his protection and does not leave him to others.

God the Exalted said: ﴿And if you are patient and fear God, their scheming will not harm you at all﴾

And the Prophet ﷺ said to Abdullah ibn Abbas: "Guard God and He will guard you; guard God and you will find Him before you."

Whoever guards God, God guards him and he finds Him before him wherever he turns. Whoever has God as his guardian and before him, of whom will he be afraid? And of whom will he be wary?

The third means: patience toward his enemy, not fighting him, not complaining about him, and not even entertaining in himself the thought of harming him. Nothing gains victory over an envier and enemy like patience with him and reliance upon God, and not deeming his delay and transgression to be long. For whenever he transgresses against him, his transgression becomes an army and strength for the transgressed-against envied one, by which the transgressor fights himself, while he is unaware. His transgression is arrows he shoots from himself at himself.

If the one transgressed against saw this, his transgression against him would delight him.

But due to the weakness of his insight, he sees only the image of the transgression, not its end and outcome.

God the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, then is transgressed against, God will surely help him﴾

If God has guaranteed him victory, although he had first taken his right, how much more so for one who has not taken any of his right, but was transgressed against while he remained patient? Of sins, none is quicker in punishment than transgression and severing of kinship. And God's established way has preceded: that if one mountain transgressed against another, the transgressor of the two would be crushed to dust.

The fourth means: reliance upon God. Whoever relies upon God, He is sufficient for him.

Reliance is among the strongest means by which a servant repels what he cannot bear of people's harm, oppression and aggression, and it is among the strongest causes in this. For God is sufficient for him, that is, sufficient for him. Whoever has God as his sufficiency and protector, his enemy has no hope of him, and he is harmed only by an unavoidable harm, like heat and cold, hunger and thirst. As for his enemy harming him in a way that achieves his aim, that will never happen.

There is a difference between harm which outwardly is harm to him, but in reality is a kindness to him and a harm to the one who inflicts it, and the harm by which the enemy seeks to satisfy himself. One of the early scholars said:

God has made for every deed a recompense of its kind, and made the recompense for reliance upon Him the very sufficiency of His sufficing His servant. So He said: ﴿And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him﴾

He did not say, "We will give him such-and-such a reward," as He said regarding deeds. Rather, He made Himself the sufficiency, guardian and protector of His servant who relies upon Him. So if the servant truly relied upon God, and the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them were to plot against him, his Lord would make for him a way out of it, and would suffice him and help him.

We have mentioned the reality of reliance, its benefits, the greatness of its profit, and the servant's great need of it in "The Book of the Sacred Opening" (Kitab al-Fath al-Qudsi). There we mentioned the corruption of one who makes it among the "causal stations," and that it is a station of the common folk, and we refuted his saying in many ways. We explained that it is among the most sublime stations of the knowers (al-'arifun), that the higher a servant's station, the greater and more intense his need for reliance, and that his reliance is in proportion to his faith.

What is intended here is only mentioning the means by which the evil of the envier, the one who casts the evil eye, the sorcerer and the transgressor is averted.

The fifth means: emptying the heart of preoccupation with him and of thinking about him, and intending to erase him from his mind whenever he occurs to him. He should not turn to him, nor fear him, nor fill his heart with thoughts of him.

This is among the most beneficial remedies and the strongest means of aiding the averting of his evil. For this is like one whom his enemy seeks to seize in order to hold and harm him. If he does not expose himself to him and does not grapple with him, but withdraws from him, the enemy cannot prevail over him. But if they grapple and each clings to the other, harm results. So it is with spirits as well. When he attaches his spirit to him and fixes it upon him, while the envier's and transgressor's spirit is attached to him, awake and in dreams, never relenting, wishing that the two spirits should grapple and cling together, then when each spirit clings to the other, no rest is found, and harm persists until one of them perishes.

But if he tears his spirit away from him, and protects it from thinking of him and clinging to him, and does not let him occur to his mind, then whenever a thought of him occurs, he hastens to erase that thought and occupy himself with what is more beneficial to him and more fitting for him, the envier and transgressor is left devouring himself. For envy is like fire: when it finds nothing to consume, it consumes itself.

This is a matter of great benefit, which only those of noble souls and lofty aspirations attain, and between the shrewd and intelligent man and it lies the step until he tastes its sweetness, goodness and bliss. It is as if he sees that the greatest torment of the heart and spirit is to be occupied with his enemy and to have his spirit attached to him, and he sees nothing more painful to his spirit than that. And only the tranquil, peaceful, gentle souls believe this, those who are content with God's guardianship of them and know that His victory for them is better than their own victory for themselves. So they trust God, find calm in Him, are reassured by Him, and know that His guarantee is true, His promise is sincere, that none is more faithful to his covenant than God, and none more truthful in speech than He.

They know that His victory for them is stronger, more firmly established, more lasting, and of greater benefit than their victory for themselves, or the victory of a created being like them on their behalf. And none can attain this except through the sixth means: turning to God, sincerity toward Him, making His love, His pleasure and turning to Him the place of the thoughts of his soul and its wishes, such that they creep into them gradually, little by little, until he overcomes them, overwhelms them and removes them entirely. Then his thoughts, his anxieties and his wishes all remain in what the Lord loves, drawing near to Him, seeking to win His favour, pleading with Him, and remembering Him, as the perfectly loving lover remembers his beloved who has been kind to him and whose heart is filled with his love. His heart cannot turn away from remembering Him, nor his spirit turn away from loving Him. When he becomes so, how could he accept for his soul that the house of his thoughts and his heart should be populated with thinking about his envier and transgressor, and the way to revenge upon him, and plotting against him? This is something that only a ruined heart in which the love and reverence of God and the seeking of His pleasure have not dwelt can contain. Indeed, if a phantom of that touches it and passes by its gate from outside, the guards of its heart call out: "Beware of the King's sanctuary! Go to the inns, where whoever comes alights and lodges. What have you to do with the palace of the sultan, around which the watch is posted, the guards are placed, and which is surrounded by the wall?"

God the Exalted related the words of His enemy Iblis: ﴿So by Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾ Then God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾

And He said: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate partners with Him﴾

And He said concerning the truthful Joseph ﷺ: ﴿Thus, that We might avert from him evil and immorality; indeed, he was of Our sincere servants﴾

How great is the happiness of one who enters this fortress and becomes within the watch-post! He has taken refuge in a fortress for which there is no fear for whoever takes refuge in it, no loss for whoever shelters in it, and no hope for the enemy to approach him. ﴿That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty﴾.

The seventh means: sincerely repenting to God from the sins that have empowered his enemies over him.

For God the Exalted says: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you, it is because of what your hands have earned﴾

And He said to the best of creation, who are the companions of His Prophet apart from him ﷺ: ﴿Why, when a disaster struck you, though you had struck twice as much, did you say, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾

No one is empowered over a servant to harm him except because of a sin he knows or does not know. The sins he does not know are many times more than those he knows, and what he forgets of what he has done is many times more than what he remembers.

In the well-known supplication: "O God, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know."

So what a servant needs to seek forgiveness for of what he does not know is many times over what he knows. No harmer is empowered over him except because of a sin.

One of the early scholars met a man who was harsh with him and abused him. He said to him: "Wait until I enter the house, then I will come out to you." He entered, prostrated to God, humbled himself before Him, repented, and turned to his Lord. Then he came out to him and the man said: "What have you done?" He said: "I repented to God from the sin for which He empowered you over me."

We will mention, God willing, that there is no evil in existence except sins and what they necessitate. So when a servant is cured of sins, he is cured of their consequences. Therefore, when a servant is transgressed against, harmed, and his adversaries prevail over him, there is nothing more beneficial to him than sincere repentance.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 113, verse 5 (part 3 of 5):**

The sign of his happiness is that he turns his thought and attention upon himself, his sins and his faults, and occupies himself with them, with reforming them and with repenting from them. Then no leisure remains in him to reflect on what has befallen him. Rather, he himself undertakes repentance and the reform of his faults. Allah undertakes his support, his protection and the warding off of harm from him, without doubt. How happy is such a servant, and how blessed is the calamity that befell him! How good is its effect upon him! But success and right guidance are in the hand of Allah. None can withhold what He gives, and none can give what He withholds. Not everyone is granted success in this. It requires knowledge of it, the will for it, and the ability to achieve it. There is no power and no strength except with Allah.

**The eighth cause: charity and doing good, as much as one is able.** Indeed, these have a remarkable effect in warding off affliction, in repelling the evil eye and the harm of the envier. Even if there were no proof for this except the experience of nations, past and present, it would suffice. The evil eye, envy and harm hardly ever gain power over a doer of good who gives charity. If something of that should befall him, he is treated in it with gentleness, help and support, and he has in it a praiseworthy outcome.

The doer of good who gives charity is under the protection of his good deeds and his charity. From Allah he has a protecting shield and an impregnable fortress.

In sum, gratitude is the guardian of blessing against everything that could be a cause of its removal.

Among the strongest causes (of harm) is the envy of the envier and of the one who casts the evil eye. Such a person does not slacken or tire, and his heart is not cooled until the blessing is removed from the one envied. Then his groaning subsides and his fire is extinguished, may Allah never extinguish it. No servant guards the blessing of Allah like guarding it through gratitude, and no one exposes it to removal like acting in it through disobedience to Allah, which is ingratitude for the blessing. And that is a door to ingratitude towards the Benefactor.

The doer of good who gives charity employs troops and an army that fight on his behalf while he sleeps on his bed. Whoever has no troops or army, and has an enemy, will soon be overcome by his enemy, even if the time of victory is delayed. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

**The ninth cause:** This is one of the most difficult causes for the soul and the hardest on it, and only one whose share from Allah is great is granted success in it. It is extinguishing the fire of the envier, the transgressor and the one who harms you, by doing good to him. Whenever he increases in harm, evil, transgression and envy, you increase in goodness towards him, in sincere counsel for him and in compassion for him. I do not think you would believe that this could happen, let alone that you would practise it.

Now listen to the words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And good and evil are not equal. Repel (evil) with that which is better, and then the one between whom and you there is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune. And if an evil suggestion from Satan should prompt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (Fussilat 41:34–36)

And He says: ﴿They will be given their reward twice, because they were patient, and they repel evil with good, and they spend from what We have provided them.﴾ (al-Qasas 28:54)

Consider the state of the Prophet (ﷺ) when his people beat him until they drew blood. He began wiping the blood from himself and saying: "O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know." (Bukhari and Muslim)

How did he gather in these words four stations of goodness, by which he met their great harm to him?

The first: his pardon for them. The second: his asking forgiveness for them. The third: his excusing them, saying that they do not know. The fourth: his appeal to their hearts by attributing them to himself.

He said, "Forgive my people," as a man says to one who intercedes with him for someone connected to him: "This is my son, this is my servant, this is my companion, so grant him to me."

Now listen to what makes this easy for the soul, pleasant for it and gladdens it with it.

Know that you have sins between you and Allah, of whose consequences you are afraid, and you hope that He will pardon them, forgive you and grant them to you. Yet with all this He does not limit Himself to mere pardon and forgiveness. He bestows favour and honour upon you, and brings to you benefits and goodness beyond what you hope for. So if you hope for this from your Lord, and you love that your wrongdoing be met with it, how much more worthy and deserving are you to treat His creatures with it, and to meet their wrongdoing with it, so that Allah may treat you in that manner? For the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Just as you act with people in their wrongdoing against you, Allah will act with you regarding your sins and your wrongdoing, as a just recompense. So then, take revenge, or pardon; do good, or leave it. As you judge, so you will be judged, and as you do to His servants, He will do to you.

Whoever contemplates this meaning and occupies his thought with it, doing good to one who wrongs him becomes easy for him.

Along with this, he gains through it the victory of Allah and His special companionship, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the one who complained to him that he was kind to his relatives while they wronged him. He said: "Allah's support will remain with you as long as you act in this way."

Along with this, he hastens to gain the praise of people, and they will all side with him against his opponent, for everyone who hears that he is kind to someone who wrongs him finds his heart, his wish and his aspiration inclined towards the one who does good rather than the one who does wrong. This is an innate matter, with which Allah has created His servants. Thus, through this goodness, he has employed an army whom he does not know and who do not know him, and who do not want from him any grant of land or bread.

Along with all this, he must face his enemy and envier in one of two states. Either he will master him through his goodness, enslaving him, bringing him to submission and humiliation, and keeping people with him. Or he will crush his liver and cut off his root, if the other persists in wronging him. For he makes him taste, through his goodness, many times more than what he could inflict upon him through retaliation. Whoever has tested this knows its true reality. Allah is the One who grants success and help. In His hand is all good; there is no god but Him. He is the One asked to make us and our brothers use this, by His bounty and generosity.

In sum, this station contains benefits exceeding one hundred for the servant, both immediate and deferred. We shall mention them in another place, if Allah wills.

**The tenth cause:** This comprehends all of these, and all these causes revolve around it. It is making tawhid (monotheism) pure, and travelling with thought through the causes to the Mighty, Wise Causer. It is knowing that these instruments are like the movements of the winds, which are in the hand of their Mover, their Originator and their Creator, and they neither harm nor benefit except by His permission. He is the One who does good to His servant through them, and He alone, with no one else, turns them away from him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him. And if He wills good for you, there is none who can repel His bounty.﴾ (Yunus 10:107)

The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them: "Know that if the whole community gathered to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with what Allah has written for you. And if they gathered to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with what Allah has written against you." (Tirmidhi)

When the servant makes tawhid pure, the fear of anything other than Allah leaves his heart, and his enemy becomes easier for him than to fear him alongside Allah. Rather, he singles out Allah for fear, and He has secured him from it. His concern with the enemy leaves his heart, and his preoccupation with him and his thought about him leave too. He devotes himself to Allah in love, fear, turning in repentance and trust, and he is occupied with Him instead of with others. He sees that devoting his thought to the matter of his enemy, fearing him, and being preoccupied with him is a deficiency in his tawhid. Otherwise, if he had made his tawhid pure, he would have had an absorbing occupation in it. Allah undertakes his protection and his defence, for Allah defends those who believe. So if he is a believer in Allah, then Allah defends him without doubt, and the extent of Allah's defence is in proportion to his faith.

If his faith is perfect, Allah's defence of him is most complete. If his faith is mixed, the defence is mixed for him. If he is partly devoted to Allah, Allah is partly with him. Whoever turns away from Allah entirely, Allah turns away from him entirely. Whoever is sometimes devoted and sometimes not, Allah is with him sometimes and not other times.

Thus tawhid is Allah's greatest fortress; whoever enters it is among the secure. One of the early Muslims said: "Whoever fears Allah, everything fears him. Whoever does not fear Allah, He makes him fear everything."

These are ten causes by which the evil of the envier, the one who casts the evil eye, and the sorcerer is repelled. There is nothing more beneficial for him than turning to Allah, coming to Him, trusting in Him, relying on Him, and not fearing anything along with Him. Rather, his fear should be of Him alone, and he should hope in none other than Him. He should not attach his heart to anything else, nor seek help from anyone other than Him, nor hope for anything except Him. Whenever he attaches his heart to other than Allah, and hopes in it and fears it, he is left to it and abandoned on its account. Whoever fears something other than Allah, it is given power over him. Whoever hopes for something other than Allah is abandoned on its account and deprived of its good. This is the way of Allah with His creation, and you will never find any change in the way of Allah.

**(Section)**

You have now come to know some of what this surah contains of beneficial and important principles, which the servant cannot do without in his religion or his worldly life. It indicates that the souls and the eyes of envious people have an effect, and that satanic spirits have an effect through sorcery and blowing into knots.

On this matter the world has divided into four groups.

One group denied both this and that. They are of two kinds.

The first kind acknowledged the existence of rational souls and jinn, but denied that they have any effect at all. This is the view of a group of the theologians (mutakallimun) who deny causes, powers and influences.

The second kind denied their existence altogether, saying that there is no existence for the human soul apart from this perceptible body and its attributes and accidents alone, and no existence for jinn and devils apart from accidents subsisting in them. This is the view of many of the materialist naturalists and others among the atheists who claim to be Muslims. It is also the view of some deviant theologians whom the early Muslims blamed, and whom they testified were innovators and misguided.

The second group denied the existence of the human soul as separate from the body, but acknowledged the existence of jinn and devils. This is the view of many of the theologians, including the Mu'tazilah and others.

The third group held the opposite: they affirmed the existence of the rational soul as separate from the body, but denied the existence of jinn and devils. They claimed that the soul does not go beyond the powers and attributes of the soul itself. This is the view of many of the Islamic philosophers and others.

These say that the strange influences and extraordinary events found in the world are from the influences of the soul. They make sorcery and soothsaying entirely from the influence of the soul alone, without any separate devil as intermediary. Ibn Sina and his followers hold this view, to the extent that they place the miracles of the messengers within this category. They say that these are only the influences of the soul upon the matter of the world.

These people are unbelievers by the consensus of the adherents of the religions. They are not followers of the messengers at all.

The fourth group, who are the followers of the messengers and the people of truth, acknowledged the existence of the rational soul as separate from the body, acknowledged the existence of jinn and devils, and affirmed what Allah the Exalted has affirmed of their attributes and their evil. They sought refuge in Allah from it, and they knew that none protects them from it or grants them refuge except Allah.

These are the people of truth. Whoever is other than them is either immersed in falsehood, or has a mixture of falsehood and truth. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.

This is what Allah has facilitated of the discussion on surah al-Falaq.

**[Section: On his guidance (ﷺ) in treating one afflicted by the evil eye]**

**Section**

Sections on his guidance (ﷺ) in treatment through the divine spiritual remedies, both single and compounded from them, and from natural remedies.

**Section**

On his guidance (ﷺ) in treating one afflicted by the evil eye.

Muslim narrated in his Sahih from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real. If anything could outrun the decree, the evil eye would outrun it."

Also in his Sahih, from Anas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) "permitted ruqyah (spiritual incantation) for the sting, for the evil eye and for the ant bite."

In the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real."

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The one who casts the evil eye was ordered to perform ablution, and then the one afflicted by it would wash with it."

In the two Sahihs, from A'ishah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered me, or ordered that we seek ruqyah for the evil eye."

Tirmidhi mentioned, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Urwah ibn Amir, from Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah al-Zurqi, that Asma' bint Umays said: "O Messenger of Allah, the children of Ja'far are afflicted by the evil eye. Shall I seek ruqyah for them?" He said: "Yes, for if anything could outrun the decree, the evil eye would outrun it." Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: "Amir ibn Rabi'ah saw Sahl ibn Hunayf bathing, and said: 'By Allah, I have never seen anything like today, nor a skin as soft as a hidden maiden's.' So Sahl was struck down. Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him, and he (ﷺ) became angry with Amir and said: 'Why does one of you kill his brother? Did you not say, Bless him? Wash for him.' So Amir washed for him his face, his hands, his elbows, his knees, the tips of his feet, and the inside of his waist-wrap, in a vessel. Then it was poured over him, and he went out with the people."

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, also narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl, from his father, this hadith, and in it he said: "The evil eye is real. Perform ablution for him," so he performed ablution for him.

Abd al-Razzaq mentioned, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, in marfu' form: "The evil eye is real. If anything could outrun the decree, the evil eye would outrun it. And when one of you is asked to wash, let him wash."

Its chain is sahih.

Al-Zuhri said: "The one who casts the evil eye is ordered to take a vessel, put his palm in it, rinse his mouth, spit it back into the vessel, wash his face in the vessel, then put his left hand in and pour onto his right knee in the vessel, then put his right hand in and pour onto his left knee, then wash the inside of his waist-wrap. The vessel is not placed on the ground. Then it is poured in one pouring over the head of the afflicted man from behind him."

The evil eye is of two kinds: a human evil eye and a jinn evil eye. It is established from Umm Salamah that the Prophet (ﷺ) saw in her house a girl with a discoloration (safa'ah) on her face, and he said: "Seek ruqyah for her, for there is a gaze (nazrah) upon her."

Al-Husayn ibn Mas'ud al-Farra' said: His words "safa'ah" mean a gaze, that is, from the jinn. He means that she was afflicted by an evil eye from the gaze of the jinn, which is more piercing than the points of spears.

It is mentioned from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The evil eye can bring a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot."

From Abu Sa'id, that the Prophet (ﷺ) "used to seek refuge from the jinn and from the evil eye of humans."

A group of people whose share of hearing and reason is small denied the reality of the evil eye and said: It is only illusions with no reality. These are among the most ignorant of people regarding revelation and reason, the most veiled, the most crude in nature, and the furthest from knowledge of spirits and souls, their attributes, their actions and their influences. Yet the wise of the nations, despite their differing religions and sects, do not deny or reject the matter of the evil eye, although they differ about the cause and manner of its influence.

One group said: When the soul of the one who casts the evil eye takes on a bad state, a poisonous force emanates from his eye and reaches the one he gazes at, and he is harmed. They said: This is not strange, just as it is not strange that a poisonous force can emanate from a snake and reach a person, so that he dies. This is well known of a type of snake: when its gaze falls upon a person, he dies. Likewise the one who casts the evil eye.

Another group said: It is not unlikely that subtle substances invisible to the eye may emanate from the eyes of some people, reach the one they gaze at, penetrate the pores of his body, and harm him.

And another group said: God has established the custom of creating harm, whatever He wills, when the eye of the one who causes the evil eye (al-'a'in) meets the one he afflicts, without the latter having any power, cause, or influence at all. This is the position of those who deny causes (al-asbab), powers (al-quwa), and influences (al-ta'thirat) in the world. They have closed to themselves the door of causes and effects (al-'ilal wa'l-ta'thirat wa'l-asbab), and they have opposed all the people of reason.

There is no doubt that God, glory be to Him, created in bodies and in souls various powers and natures, and placed in many of them properties (khawass) and qualities that have effect. No one of reason can deny the influence of souls upon bodies, for this is a matter that is observed and perceived by the senses.

You see how the face reddens intensely when someone whom one respects and feels shy before looks at it, and how it turns intensely pale when the gaze of someone one fears falls upon it. People have witnessed one who falls ill from a look and whose strength is weakened. All of this happens through the influence of souls. Because of the strong connection of the soul with the eye, the act is attributed to the eye, though it is not the actual agent; the influence belongs to the soul. Souls differ in their natures, powers, qualities, and properties, so the soul of the envier (al-hasid) harms the envied (al-mahsud) with clear harm.

For this reason God, glory be to Him, commanded His Messenger to seek refuge with Him from its evil.
