The influence of the envier on the harm done to the envied is a matter that none denies except one who has stepped outside the reality of humanity. This is the root of affliction by the evil eye. The evil, envious soul takes on an evil quality and confronts the envied one, and influences him through that property. The thing most similar to this is the viper, for its poison is latent within it in potential, and when it confronts its enemy, a wrathful power is emitted from it, and it takes on an evil, harmful quality.

Among these [effects] is that the quality intensifies and grows strong enough to cause the miscarriage of a fetus.

Among them is that it affects the eyesight (tams al-basar), as the Prophet (ﷺ) said concerning the abtar (short-tailed) and the dhu'l-tufyatayn (two-striped) among snakes: "They seek out the eyesight and cause miscarriage."

Among them is that its quality affects a person merely by seeing, without contact, because of the extreme evil of that soul and its harmful evil quality. The influence is not confined to physical contact, as one believes who has little knowledge of nature (al-tabi'a) and of the Sharia. Rather, the influence sometimes occurs through contact, sometimes through confrontation, sometimes through sight, sometimes through the soul's turning toward the one it affects, sometimes through supplications, incantations (ruqa), and seeking refuge (ta'awwudhat), and sometimes through imagination and fancy. The soul of the one who causes the evil eye does not depend on sight for its influence; he may even be blind, and when a thing is described to him, his soul influences it even though he has not seen it. Many of those who cause the evil eye influence the one afflicted by description without seeing him. God, Exalted, has said to His Prophet: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the Reminder﴾ [al-Qalam: 51].

And He said: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He created, and from the evil of darkness when it settles, and from the evil of the blowers in knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies﴾ [al-Falaq: 1-5].

Every one who causes the evil eye is an envier, but not every envier causes the evil eye. Since the envier is more general than the one who causes the evil eye, seeking refuge from the envier is seeking refuge from the one who causes the evil eye. These are arrows that come out from the soul of the envier and the one who causes the evil eye toward the envied and the afflicted: they sometimes strike and sometimes miss. If they meet him unprotected, with no shield, they will certainly affect him. If they meet him wary and armed, with no opening for the arrows, they will not affect him. Sometimes the arrows are returned to their owner. This is exactly like physical shooting. The former is of souls and spirits, and the latter is of bodies and forms.

Its origin is the admiration of the one who causes the evil eye for a thing, then his evil soul follows, then he seeks help in executing its poison by a glance at the one afflicted. A man may cause the evil eye to himself, and he may cause it without intending to, by his very nature. This is the worst kind of human being. Our companions and other jurists have said that whoever is known for this should be detained by the ruler, and be given what he needs to live on until death. This is certainly the correct position.

[Section: Treatment of the afflicted by seeking refuge and incantations]

Section

The purpose here is the Prophetic treatment of this affliction, which has several kinds. Abu Dawud recorded in his Sunan from Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: "We passed by a stream and I entered it and bathed in it, and I came out with a fever. This was reported to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: 'Order Abu Thabit to seek refuge.' I said: 'O my master! Are incantations (ruqa) beneficial?' He said: 'There is no incantation except for the evil eye (nafs), or venom, or a sting.'"

Al-nafs means the evil eye. It is said: "Such-and-such was struck by an evil eye (nafs)," meaning by an eye (ayn). The one who causes the evil eye is called al-nafis. Al-lad'a, with an unpointed dal and a pointed ghayn, is the sting of a scorpion and the like.

Among the incantations and ruqa is frequent recitation of the two Mu'awwidhatayn, al-Fatiha, and Ayat al-Kursi. Among them also are the Prophetic seekings of refuge, such as: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He created."

And such as: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from every devil and venomous creature, and from every harmful evil eye."

And such as: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of God which neither the righteous nor the wicked can surpass, from the evil of what He created, what He produced, and what He originated, and from the evil of what descends from the sky, and from the evil of what ascends into it, and from the evil of what He produced in the earth, and from the evil of what comes out of it, and from the evil of the trials of night and day, and from the evil of nocturnal visitors, except a visitor who visits with good, O Most Merciful."

Among them: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from His wrath and His punishment, and from the evil of His servants, and from the promptings of the devils and their presence."

Among them: "O God, I seek refuge in Your noble Face and Your perfect words from the evil of what You hold by its forelock. O God, You remove sin and debt. O God, Your army is not defeated, and Your promise is not broken. Glory be to You and praise be to You."

Among them: "I seek refuge in the Face of the Mighty God, than which nothing is greater, and in His perfect words which neither the righteous nor the wicked can surpass, and in the Beautiful Names of God, those I know and those I do not know, from the evil of what He created, produced, and originated, and from the evil of every possessor of evil whose evil I cannot bear, and from the evil of every possessor of evil whose forelock You hold. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path."

Among them: "O God, You are my Lord, there is no god but You. In You I have put my trust, and You are the Lord of the Mighty Throne. Whatever God wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. There is no power and no strength except through God. I know that God is over all things powerful, and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge and has counted all things in number. O God, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul, and from the evil of Satan and his association, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path."

If he wishes, he may say: "I have taken refuge in God, there is no god but He, my God and the God of all things. I have held fast to my Lord and the Lord of all things. I have put my trust in the Living who does not die. I have sought to repel evil, there is no power and no strength except through God. God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Guardian. My Lord is sufficient for me of the servants. My Creator is sufficient for me of the created. My Provider is sufficient for me of the provided. He who is sufficient for me is sufficient for me. He in whose hand is the dominion of all things is sufficient for me, and He protects, and none can protect against Him. God is sufficient for me and enough. God hears the one who calls. There is no goal beyond God. God is sufficient for me, there is no god but Him. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."

Whoever tries these supplications and seekings of refuge will know the measure of their benefit and the great need for them. They prevent the arrival of the effect of the one who causes the evil eye, and they repel it after its arrival, in proportion to the strength of the faith of the one who recites them, the strength of his soul, his readiness, the strength of his trust in God, and the steadiness of his heart. For they are a weapon, and a weapon is only as good as the one who wields it.

[Section: What the one who causes the evil eye should say, fearing the harm of his eye]

Section

If the one who causes the evil eye fears the harm of his eye and its striking the one he looks at, let him repel its evil by saying: "O God, bless him." The Prophet (ﷺ) said this to Amir ibn Rabi'a when he afflicted Sahl ibn Hunayf with the evil eye: "Why did you not bless him?" That is, why did you not say: "O God, bless him."

Among what the striking of the evil eye is repelled by is the saying: "What God wills; there is no power except through God." Hisham ibn 'Urwa narrated from his father that when he saw something that pleased him, or entered one of his orchards, he would say: "What God wills; there is no power except through God."

Among them is the incantation of Jibril (peace be upon him) for the Prophet (ﷺ), which Muslim recorded in his Sahih:
"In the name of God I incant you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye. God heals you. In the name of God I incant you."

A group of the early generations (al-salaf) held that verses of the Qur'an should be written for him, and then he should drink them.

Mujahid said: "There is no harm in writing the Qur'an, washing it off, and giving it to the sick to drink." The same was reported from Abu Qilaba.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he ordered that a verse of the Qur'an be written for a woman whose delivery was difficult, and then it be washed off and she be given to drink.

Ayyub said: "I saw Abu Qilaba write a writing from the Qur'an, then wash it with water and give it to a man who had pain."

[Section: The afflicted person's washing for the one who causes the evil eye, and the response to those among the physicians who deny it]

Section

Among them: the one who causes the evil eye should be ordered to wash his folds (maghabin), his extremities, and the inner part of his waistcloth. Concerning this there are two opinions. One is that it is his private part. The second is that it is the inner edge of his waistcloth that touches his body on the right side. Then water is poured suddenly over the head of the afflicted person from behind. This is something that the treatment of physicians cannot reach, and whoever denies it, mocks it, doubts it, or does it as a mere experiment without believing that it benefits him, will not benefit from it.

If there are properties in nature (al-tabi'a) whose causes physicians do not know at all, and which are considered by them to be outside the measure of nature, acting through a special property, then what do their heretics and ignorant ones deny among the legal properties (al-khawass al-shar'iyya)? This is in addition to the fact that in this treatment by washing there is what sound reason witnesses to and accepts as appropriate. Know that the antidote of snake venom is in its flesh, and that the treatment of the influence of a wrathful soul is by quieting its anger and extinguishing its fire through placing your hand upon it, stroking it, and calming its anger. This is like a man who holds a flame of fire and wants to throw it at you; you pour water upon it while it is in his hand until it is extinguished. This is why the one who causes the evil eye is ordered to say: "O God, bless him," in order to repel that evil quality through supplication, which is a kindness to the afflicted person, for the cure of a thing is by its opposite.

Since this evil quality appears in the delicate parts of the body, because it seeks to penetrate, it finds nothing more delicate than the folds and the inner edge of the waistcloth, especially if it refers to the private part. When these are washed with water, its influence and action are nullified. Also, these places are associated with satanic spirits.

The purpose is that washing them with water extinguishes that fiery and venomous quality and removes its poison.

There is another matter in it: the effect of the washing reaches the heart, which is the most delicate place and the swiftest in executing [influence]. So it extinguishes that fiery and venomous quality with water, and the afflicted person is healed. This is like the case of venomous creatures: when they are killed after stinging, the effect of the sting lessens for the stung person and he finds relief, for their souls keep extending their harm after they sting and conveying it to the stung person. When they are killed, the pain subsides. This is observed. And if one of its causes is the joy of the stung person and the satisfaction of his soul in killing his enemy, then his nature becomes stronger against the pain and repels it.

In sum, the washing by the one who causes the evil eye removes that quality which emerged from him, and its washing benefits only when his soul has taken on that quality.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 113, verse 5 (part 5 of 5):

If it is asked: the connection of washing has become clear, so what is the connection of pouring that water over the one who causes the evil eye (al-mu'ayn)? It is answered: it is in the utmost connection. That water is water by which that fiery quality (al-nariyya) is extinguished, and by which that bad disposition from the agent is nullified. Just as the fiery quality that subsists in the agent is extinguished by it, so it is extinguished by it, and removed from the affected subject (al-mahall al-mutha'thir) after its contact with the influencing agent, the one who casts the evil eye. The water with which iron is quenched enters into several natural remedies that the physicians (al-atibba') have mentioned. So that by which the fiery quality of the one who casts the evil eye is extinguished is not to be denied as entering into a remedy suited to this disease.

In sum: the medicine of the naturalists (tibb al-taba'iʿiyya), and their treatment compared with the prophetic treatment, is like the medicine of the folk healers (tibb al-turuqiyya) compared with their medicine, or even less. For the gap between them and the Prophets is greater, and greater than the gap between them and the folk healers, by an amount a person cannot grasp. Thus there has become clear to you the bond of brotherhood between wisdom (al-hikma) and the revealed law (al-shar'), and that neither of them contradicts the other. God guides whom He wills to what is right, and opens to whoever persists in knocking at the door of success every door, and His is the abundant blessing and the conclusive proof.

[Section: Guarding against being struck by the evil eye by concealing the beauty of those who are feared to be affected by it]

Section

Among the treatments for this, and for guarding against it, is also concealing the beauty of those who are feared to be affected by the evil eye, with what turns it away from them. As al-Baghawi mentioned in his book Sharh al-Sunna: ʿUthman, may God be pleased with him, saw a handsome boy and said: "Blacken his nunna (dassimu nunnatahu), lest the evil eye strike him." Then he said in his explanation: the meaning of "dassimu nunnatahu" is: blacken his nunna. The nunna is the small mark (nuqra) that is on the chin of a young child.

Al-Khattabi said in his Gharib al-Hadith, from ʿUthman: that he saw a boy whom the evil eye had seized, and he said: "Blacken his nunna." Abu ʿAmr said: I asked Ahmad ibn Yahya about it, and he said: by the nunna he meant the mark that is on his chin. And al-tadsim is al-taswid (blackening). He meant: blacken that place on his chin so that it turns back the evil eye. He said: from this is the hadith of ʿAʾisha that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) "delivered a sermon one day with a black turban (ʿimama dasmaʾ) on his head," that is, a black one. He intended by it to cite the word's usage. And from this the poet took his saying:

What a need the one of perfection has
for a blemish that protects him from the evil eye.

Section: Mention of an incantation (ruqya) that turns back the evil eye

Among the incantations that turn back the evil eye is what is reported from Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Sajji, that during some of his journeys, either for the pilgrimage or for the raid, he was on a fine she-camel. There was a man in the caravan who was an evil-eye caster (ʿaʾin); he rarely looked at anything without destroying it. It was said to Abu ʿAbd Allah: guard your she-camel from the one who casts the evil eye. He said: he has no way to my she-camel. The evil-eye caster was informed of his words, so he watched for Abu ʿAbd Allah's absence and came to his baggage, looked at the she-camel, and it trembled and fell down. Abu ʿAbd Allah came and was told that the evil-eye caster had struck her, and she was as he saw. He said: point him out to me. He was pointed out, and he stood over him and said: "In the name of God, a restraining restraint, a dry stone, and a quenching flame. I have returned the eye of the one who casts it upon him and upon the dearest of people to him." Then he recited: "Look again; do you see any flaw? Then look again, twice; your sight will return to you dazzled and fatigued" (Qur'an 67:3–4). Then the two eyeballs of the evil-eye caster came out, and the she-camel stood up, with no harm to her.
